artworks.title: Telemachus and Mentor
artworks.description: Charles Monnet's illustration for Fénelon's Télémaque shows the Ithacan elder with Odysseus' son — the Homeric Mentor whose name Athena borrows when she guides Telemachus. Eighteenth-century engraving culture made this pair the emblem of wise counsel; the print is the visual root of the modern word 'mentor.'

artworks.title: Telemachus, Urged by Mentor, Leaving the Island of Calypso
artworks.description: Meynier's neoclassical canvas stages Fénelon's episode in which Mentor (Athena in disguise) pulls Telemachus away from Calypso's isle. The painting belongs to the didactic afterlife of the Odyssey's trusted friend — Mentor as the voice that turns a wandering prince toward duty.

films.title: The Odyssey
films.description: Konchalovsky's miniseries keeps Ithaca's household and Telemachus' search — the world in which Mentor stands as Odysseus' friend and Athena's chosen likeness.

popCulture.title: Les Aventures de Télémaque
popCulture.creator: François Fénelon
popCulture.description: Fénelon's didactic novel made Mentor the tutor of princes — the Homeric name that entered every European language as the word for a wise guide.

popCulture.title: mentor (word)
popCulture.description: English and many other languages took 'mentor' from the Odyssey figure — Odysseus' Ithacan friend as the common noun for a trusted adviser.
